questions.title: Compute a z-Score and Compare Two Values - compute z = (x - mu) / sigma for a given observation, then compare two z-scores to decide which is more unusual
Empirical Rule (68-95-99.7) - apply the empirical rule to estimate percentages within k SDs of the mean and a tail percentage on one side
Read the Notation - mu, sigma, and the median of X ~ N(mu, sigma)
Compute a z-Score from a Value - z = (x - mu) / sigma and its sign-and-size reading
Recover a Value from a z-Score - x = mu + z*sigma and its sign-and-size reading
Read the Sign and Size of a z-Score - how far, which direction, and the mean
The Empirical Rule Bands - the 68%, 95%, and 99.7% intervals of N(mu, sigma)
Empirical Rule Percentages - 34%, 13.5%, and 4.7% between the bands
Compare Two Distributions by z-Score - equal z-scores from differently scaled normals
